questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Endocrine glands release their secretions (hormones) without the help of any duct. For this reason they are also called:

options.text: Exocrine glands
Ductless glands
Holocrine glands
Accessory glands

solution.explanation: NCERT: endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence called ductless glands; their secretions are called hormones.
solution.why_others_wrong: Exocrine glands pour their secretions through ducts; holocrine and accessory glands are not names NCERT uses for endocrine glands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Endocrine glands and hormones
solution.final_answer: Option B: Ductless glands

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, how does the endocrine system of invertebrates compare with that of vertebrates?

options.text: Invertebrates have no hormones; all their coordination is neural
Invertebrates have more hormones than vertebrates
Invertebrates have very simple endocrine systems with few hormones
Invertebrates and vertebrates have identical endocrine systems

solution.concept: Endocrine systems of invertebrates and vertebrates
solution.explanation: NCERT: invertebrates possess very simple endocrine systems with few hormones, whereas a large number of chemicals act as hormones and provide coordination in the vertebrates.
steps: Invertebrates: very simple endocrine systems, few hormones
Vertebrates: a large number of hormones
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT says invertebrates do have hormones, only few of them, and that vertebrates have a large number of chemicals acting as hormones; so 'no hormones', 'more hormones' and 'identical systems' are all wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Endocrine glands and hormones
solution.final_answer: Option C: Invertebrates have very simple endocrine systems with few hormones

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH) is regulated by:

options.text: TSH from the anterior pituitary
The circulating levels of calcium ions
Nerve impulses from the hypothalamus
The circulating level of thyroxine

solution.explanation: NCERT: the secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions. PTH increases the Ca2+ level in the blood.
steps: Its secretion is regulated by the circulating Ca2+ level
solution.why_others_wrong: TSH regulates the thyroid, not the parathyroids; NCERT names no hypothalamic nerve control or thyroxine control for PTH - it names the blood calcium level.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The parathyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: The circulating levels of calcium ions

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons are made available for regulating the pituitary because they:

options.text: Are poured into ducts that open into the pituitary
Are carried to the pituitary by lymph vessels
Are stored in the pineal gland before release
Pass through axons and are released from the nerve endings

solution.explanation: NCERT: the hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons pass through axons and are released from their nerve endings. They reach the pituitary through a portal circulatory system.
steps: Pass through axons, released from nerve endings
solution.why_others_wrong: The hypothalamus is part of the endocrine (ductless) system, so no ducts are involved; NCERT mentions axons and a portal circulatory system, not lymph vessels or the pineal gland.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus
solution.final_answer: Option D: Pass through axons and are released from the nerve endings

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Insulin lowers the blood glucose level (hypoglycemia) because it:

options.text: Stimulates glycogenolysis in the hepatocytes
Enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, so glucose moves rapidly from blood into hepatocytes and adipocytes
Stimulates gluconeogenesis in the liver
Reduces the cellular uptake and utilisation of glucose

solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation. As a result there is a rapid movement of glucose from blood to hepatocytes and adipocytes, resulting in decreased blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia).
steps: Insulin enhances glucose uptake and utilisation
Glucose moves from blood into liver and fat cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis and reduced glucose uptake are the actions of glucagon, which raise blood glucose (hyperglycemia).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option B: Enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, so glucose moves rapidly from blood into hepatocytes and adipocytes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the portal circulatory system between the hypothalamus and the pituitary is blocked, the secretion of TSH and ACTH is affected.
Reason (R): Hypothalamic hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of anterior pituitary hormones reach the pituitary through this portal circulatory system.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Hypothalamic control of the anterior pituitary
solution.explanation: TSH and ACTH are made by the pars distalis (anterior pituitary). Their synthesis and secretion are regulated by hypothalamic hormones, which reach the pituitary through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary. Blocking this route removes the hypothalamic regulation, so A is true and R is the reason.
steps: These hormones travel by the portal system -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the very route whose blockage causes A, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hormone receptors present inside the target cells are mostly nuclear receptors.
Statement II: Hormones that interact with membrane-bound receptors mostly regulate gene expression through the interaction of the hormone-receptor complex with the genome.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors. Hormones that interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell; they generate second messengers that regulate cellular metabolism. It is the hormones with intracellular receptors (steroids, iodothyronines) that mostly regulate gene expression through the genome.
steps: Statement II: false - that is how intracellular-receptor hormones act
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II swaps the two mechanisms, so A and D are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.question_text:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Targets and nature of the pancreatic hormones
solution.explanation: NCERT: glucagon is a peptide hormone that acts mainly on the liver cells (hepatocytes). Insulin is a peptide hormone that acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes (cells of adipose tissue).
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT lines, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (cells or tissue that secrete it).

List-I:
A. Glucagon
B. Testosterone
C. Progesterone (after ovulation)
D. Noradrenaline

List-II:
I. Adrenal medulla
II. Corpus luteum
III. α-cells of the islets of Langerhans
IV. Leydig cells in the intertubular spaces of the testis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

solution.explanation: Glucagon is secreted by the α-cells of the islets of Langerhans. Testosterone (an androgen) is produced by the Leydig (interstitial) cells present in the intertubular spaces of the testis. After ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone. Noradrenaline is secreted by the adrenal medulla.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap glucagon with testosterone, progesterone with noradrenaline, or testosterone with progesterone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas; Testis; Ovary; The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following hormones interact with intracellular receptors and mostly regulate gene expression or chromosome function?

(a) Cortisol
(b) Estradiol
(c) Thyroxine (an iodothyronine)
(d) Glucagon
(e) Insulin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a) and (b) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: hormones that interact with intracellular receptors (e.g., steroid hormones, iodothyronines) mostly regulate gene expression or chromosome function. Cortisol and estradiol are steroids and thyroxine is an iodothyronine. Glucagon and insulin are peptide hormones that bind membrane-bound receptors and act through second messengers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Glucagon and insulin act through membrane-bound receptors, so any option including (d) or (e) is wrong; leaving out thyroxine ignores the iodothyronines that NCERT names.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A person with exophthalmic goitre shows loss of body weight.
Reason (R): Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism in which the basal metabolic rate is increased.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by enlargement of the thyroid, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate and weight loss. Thyroid hormones regulate the BMR; an abnormally raised BMR burns body reserves faster, which causes the weight loss.
steps: A: true (weight loss is a feature)
Raised BMR is what leads to the weight loss -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the cause of the weight loss, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A tumour of the adrenal cortex secretes too much aldosterone. Which of the following changes is expected?

options.text: Decreased reabsorption of Na+, loss of water in urine and a fall in blood pressure
Increased reabsorption of K+ and increased excretion of Na+
Increased reabsorption of Na+ and water and increased excretion of K+, tending to raise the blood pressure
A fall in blood glucose due to increased glycogenesis

solution.explanation: NCERT: aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water and the excretion of K+ and phosphate ions. It thus helps maintain electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure. Too much aldosterone therefore increases Na+ and water retention and K+ loss, which raises the body fluid volume and tends to raise the blood pressure.
steps: Aldosterone: Na+ and water reabsorbed, K+ excreted
Excess -> more Na+/water retained, more K+ lost
More fluid volume -> blood pressure tends to rise
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option is the effect of too little aldosterone; the second reverses the ions; glycogenesis is an action of insulin, not of a mineralocorticoid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Increased reabsorption of Na+ and water and increased excretion of K+, tending to raise the blood pressure

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During an operation on the thyroid, all four parathyroid glands of a patient are accidentally removed. What will happen to the blood calcium level, and why?

options.text: It falls, because bone resorption, renal reabsorption and intestinal absorption of Ca2+ are no longer stimulated by PTH
It rises, because thyrocalcitonin can no longer be secreted by the parathyroids
It remains unchanged, because blood calcium is regulated only by the pineal gland
It rises, because bone demineralisation increases

solution.explanation: PTH is the hypercalcemic hormone. It stimulates bone resorption (demineralisation), reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and absorption of Ca2+ from digested food. Without the parathyroids none of these is stimulated, so the blood Ca2+ level falls.
steps: PTH raises blood Ca2+ by three routes
solution.why_others_wrong: Thyrocalcitonin comes from the thyroid, not the parathyroids; the pineal gland does not regulate blood calcium; bone demineralisation is stimulated by PTH, so it decreases, not increases, without PTH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The parathyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: It falls, because bone resorption, renal reabsorption and intestinal absorption of Ca2+ are no longer stimulated by PTH

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following hormones tend to raise the glucose concentration of the blood, by the action stated?

(a) Glucagon, by stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis
(b) Adrenaline and noradrenaline, by stimulating the breakdown of glycogen
(c) Glucocorticoids, by stimulating gluconeogenesis
(d) Insulin, by stimulating glycogenesis in its target cells
(e) Aldosterone, by stimulating the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a) and (d) only
(a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis (hyperglycemia); catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen, increasing blood glucose; glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis. Insulin converts glucose to glycogen and lowers blood glucose. Aldosterone acts on Na+, K+, phosphate and water, not glucose.
steps: (e) false - aldosterone regulates electrolytes and water
solution.why_others_wrong: Insulin is hypoglycemic, and NCERT gives aldosterone no role in glucose handling, so options including (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas; The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (observation in a patient) with List-II (most likely cause).

List-I:
A. High blood glucose for a long time, with glucose and ketone bodies in the urine
B. Enlarged thyroid in a person whose diet is deficient in iodine
C. Abnormal growth of the body of a child to a very large size
D. Raised blood Ca2+ with excessive dissolution (demineralisation) of bone

List-II:
I. Excess secretion of parathyroid hormone
II. Hypothyroidism with goitre
III. Over-secretion of growth hormone
IV. Diabetes mellitus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

solution.explanation: Prolonged hyperglycemia with loss of glucose in urine and formation of ketone bodies is diabetes mellitus. Iodine deficiency causes hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid (goitre). Over-secretion of growth hormone causes abnormal growth of the body (gigantism). PTH stimulates bone resorption and raises blood Ca2+, so excess PTH explains raised calcium with bone demineralisation.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes give the diabetic picture to goitre, the bone change to growth hormone, or the thyroid enlargement to growth hormone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas; The thyroid gland; The pituitary gland; The parathyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: GnRH and somatostatin, both hypothalamic hormones, reach the pituitary through a portal circulatory system.
Statement II: In females, FSH induces the ovulation of the fully mature Graafian follicle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: GnRH stimulates and somatostatin inhibits pituitary secretion; hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary through a portal circulatory system and regulate the anterior pituitary. In females it is LH that induces ovulation of fully mature (Graafian) follicles and maintains the corpus luteum; FSH stimulates the growth and development of the ovarian follicles.
steps: Statement II: false - LH, not FSH, induces ovulation
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II gives LH's role to FSH, so A and D are wrong; Statement I is true, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which male accessory duct ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder?

options.text: Vasa efferentia
Vas deferens
Rete testis
Urethra

solution.explanation: NCERT: the epididymis leads to the vas deferens, which ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into the urethra as the ejaculatory duct.
steps: Vas deferens ascends to the abdomen and loops over the bladder
solution.why_others_wrong: The rete testis and vasa efferentia lie in and just outside the testis and lead to the epididymis; the urethra starts from the urinary bladder and runs through the penis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: Vas deferens

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The oviduct has three parts after the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The wider part of the oviduct, which lies between the infundibulum and the isthmus, is the:

options.text: Fimbriae
Cervix
Ampulla
Endometrium

solution.explanation: NCERT: the part of the oviduct closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. It leads to a wider part of the oviduct called the ampulla. The last part, the isthmus, has a narrow lumen and joins the uterus.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fimbriae are finger-like projections on the edges of the infundibulum; the cervix and the endometrium are parts of the uterus, not of the oviduct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Ampulla

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the male sex accessory ducts (rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens) function to:

options.text: Produce the sperms by meiosis
Synthesise and secrete the androgens
Provide nutrition to the germ cells inside the seminiferous tubules
Store and transport the sperms from the testis to the outside through the urethra

solution.concept: Role of the male accessory ducts
solution.explanation: NCERT: these ducts store and transport the sperms from the testis to the outside through the urethra.
steps: Accessory ducts: store and transport sperms
solution.why_others_wrong: Sperms are produced in the seminiferous tubules, androgens by the Leydig cells, and nutrition to germ cells is provided by the Sertoli cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Store and transport the sperms from the testis to the outside through the urethra

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the parts of the female reproductive system, together with a pair of mammary glands, are integrated structurally and functionally to support:

options.text: Ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care
Only the production of ova
Only the secretion of female sex hormones
Spermatogenesis and insemination

solution.concept: Integration of the female reproductive system
solution.explanation: NCERT: the female reproductive system (ovaries, oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and external genitalia) along with a pair of mammary glands is integrated structurally and functionally to support the processes of ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care.
steps: Female system + mammary glands work together
They support ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT lists the whole range of processes, not only ovum or hormone production; spermatogenesis is a male process.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The ovaries are the primary female sex organs. Besides producing the female gamete (ovum), they produce several:

options.text: Gonadotropins such as LH and FSH
Steroid hormones (ovarian hormones)
Placental hormones such as hCG and hPL
Releasing hormones such as GnRH

solution.explanation: NCERT: the ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones (ovarian hormones).
solution.why_others_wrong: LH and FSH come from the anterior pituitary, hCG and hPL from the placenta, and GnRH from the hypothalamus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: Steroid hormones (ovarian hormones)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A spermatogonium divides by mitosis three times in succession. Assume that every cell so formed becomes a primary spermatocyte and completes spermatogenesis normally. How many spermatozoa are formed in all?

solution.explanation: Three mitotic divisions give 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cells, all primary spermatocytes. Each primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division to give two secondary spermatocytes, which undergo the second meiotic division to give four spermatids; each spermatid becomes one spermatozoon by spermiogenesis.
solution.shortcut: Sperms = 2^n x 4 for n mitotic divisions.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 counts only the primary spermatocytes; 16 stops at the secondary spermatocytes; 12 multiplies the number of divisions (3) by 4.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: 32

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Spermatids are haploid cells.
Reason (R): Spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa by the process called spermiogenesis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Ploidy of spermatids versus their fate
solution.explanation: Spermatids are haploid because they are formed by the second meiotic division of the haploid secondary spermatocytes (after the first meiotic division halved the chromosome number). R is a true NCERT statement about what spermatids later become; it says nothing about how their chromosome number was halved.
steps: R describes their later change, not why they are haploid
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermiogenesis changes the shape of the cell, not its chromosome number, so R cannot explain A (option A wrong); both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage, whereas spermatogenesis begins at puberty.
Statement II: In the human female, the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division before birth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary; spermatogenesis begins at puberty. The primary oocytes enter prophase-I and get temporarily arrested; the first meiotic division is completed only within the tertiary follicle, long after birth.
steps: Statement II: false - meiosis I is completed in the tertiary follicle
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II is false, so A and D are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The second polar body is formed only after a sperm enters the secondary oocyte.
Statement II: The zygote formed by the fusion of the haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum is diploid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Completion of meiosis and the zygote
solution.explanation: NCERT: entry of the sperm induces completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte; this second meiotic division is unequal and gives a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid). The haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum then fuse to form a diploid zygote.
steps: Statement I: true (sperm entry triggers meiosis II)
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (phase or time of the cycle) with List-II (hormonal event).

List-I:
A. Follicular phase
B. Middle of the cycle (about the 14th day)
C. Luteal phase
D. Menstrual phase of the next cycle (no fertilisation)

List-II:
I. Rapid secretion of LH (LH surge)
II. Large amounts of progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum
III. Rising secretion of estrogens by the growing follicles
IV. The corpus luteum has degenerated and the endometrium disintegrates

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

solution.explanation: During the follicular phase the gonadotropins rise gradually and stimulate the growing follicles to secrete estrogens. LH and FSH peak in the middle of the cycle; the rapid secretion of LH (LH surge) induces ovulation. In the luteal phase the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone. Without fertilisation the corpus luteum degenerates, the endometrium disintegrates and menstruation follows.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes put the LH surge in the follicular phase, place corpus luteum degeneration in the luteal phase, or give the corpus luteum's progesterone to the follicular phase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the human female reproductive system are correct?

(a) The ovaries are located one on each side of the lower abdomen.
(b) The oviducts extend from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus.
(c) The uterus is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.
(d) The cavity of the cervix (cervical canal), along with the vagina, forms the birth canal.
(e) The fimbriae are finger-like projections on the edges of the isthmus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

(e) false - oxytocin comes from the maternal pituitary

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An ovum is released at ovulation, but no sperms reach the ampullary region while the ovum is there. According to NCERT, which of the following follows?

The ovum is fertilised later in the uterus during the next cycle
The corpus luteum persists and the woman stops menstruating

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements comparing spermatogenesis and oogenesis in humans are correct?

(a) Both processes involve the first and the second meiotic divisions.
(b) A primary spermatocyte gives rise to four spermatozoa, whereas a primary oocyte gives rise to only one large functional female gamete.
(c) The first meiotic division is equal in spermatogenesis but unequal in oogenesis.
(d) Both spermatogonia and oogonia are haploid cells.
(e) New oogonia continue to be formed in the ovary throughout the reproductive life of a woman.

(a), (c) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: In spermatogenesis a primary spermatocyte completes meiosis I to give two equal haploid secondary spermatocytes, which give four spermatids and hence four sperms. In oogenesis meiosis I is unequal (large secondary oocyte and tiny first polar body) and meiosis II is also unequal (ootid and second polar body), so one functional gamete results. Spermatogonia (46 chromosomes) and oogonia are diploid. No more oogonia are formed or added after birth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a man, all the vasa efferentia of each testis are completely blocked, but the seminiferous tubules and all the accessory glands are normal. Which of the following is expected?

options.text: No sperms are formed at all, because the seminiferous tubules cannot function
Sperms reach the urethra normally through the rete testis
Sperms are formed but cannot reach the epididymis, so the ejaculate lacks sperms though seminal plasma is still produced
No semen of any kind is ejaculated, because seminal plasma is made in the testis

solution.explanation: Sperms formed in the seminiferous tubules pass through the rete testis and vasa efferentia to the epididymis and vas deferens. A block at the vasa efferentia stops sperms before the epididymis. Seminal plasma, however, comes from the accessory glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral glands), which are normal, so an ejaculate is still formed but lacks sperms.
steps: Path: tubules -> rete testis -> vasa efferentia -> epididymis
Block -> sperms cannot reach the epididymis
Accessory glands normal -> seminal plasma still formed
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermatogenesis in the tubules is unaffected; the rete testis lies before the vasa efferentia, so sperms cannot bypass the block; seminal plasma comes from the accessory glands, not the testis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Sperms are formed but cannot reach the epididymis, so the ejaculate lacks sperms though seminal plasma is still produced

A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

Immediately after implantation the inner cell mass differentiates into an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm; a mesoderm soon appears between them. The three layers give rise to all tissues (organs) in adults. Chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated and jointly form the placenta.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the trophoblast with the inner cell mass, the inner cell mass with the germ layers, or the trophoblast with the placenta.

questions.question_text: A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles, A and a. The frequency of the AA genotype is 0.49. What fraction of the individuals carry at least one copy of allele a?

solution.explanation: Individuals with at least one a allele are Aa and aa, i.e., everyone except AA. Since p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1, their frequency is 1 - p^2 = 1 - 0.49 = 0.51. (Check: p = 0.7, q = 0.3; 2pq = 0.42, q^2 = 0.09; 0.42 + 0.09 = 0.51.)
steps: Carriers of a = Aa + aa = 1 - AA
solution.shortcut: Everyone who is not AA carries a: 1 - p^2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.42 counts only heterozygotes; 0.09 counts only aa; 0.30 is the allele frequency q, not a genotype frequency.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option D: 0.51

questions.question_text: In a population of 400 individuals, the genotypes for a gene with alleles A and a are 160 AA, 160 Aa and 80 aa. 160; the population is in equilibrium
96; the observed 160 is more than expected
200; the observed 160 is fewer than expected

Which of the following statements about vaccination are correct?

(a) A preparation of antigenic proteins of a pathogen, or of inactivated/weakened pathogens, is introduced into the body.
(b) The antibodies produced in the body neutralise the pathogenic agents during actual infection.
(c) Vaccines generate memory B and T-cells that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure.
(d) Vaccination provides passive immunity.
(e) Vaccines are preferred when a quick immune response is needed, as in tetanus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(c), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: in vaccination, a preparation of antigenic proteins of a pathogen or inactivated/weakened pathogen (vaccine) is introduced; the antibodies produced neutralise the pathogenic agents during actual infection, and vaccines generate memory B and T-cells. The body makes its own antibodies, so this is active immunity. For a quick response, as in tetanus, preformed antibodies or antitoxin are injected (passive immunisation).
steps: (e) false - preformed antibodies are used for quick response
solution.why_others_wrong: Vaccination is active, and the quick response in tetanus needs preformed antibodies, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Vaccination and immunisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): HIV can be transmitted by sharing infected needles, as in intravenous drug abusers.
Reason (R): HIV is a member of the retrovirus group, having an envelope enclosing an RNA genome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Transmission of HIV versus its structure
solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. HIV spreads by sharing infected needles because the virus is carried in the infected blood on the needle. R describes the structure of the virus (retrovirus, RNA genome); this is true of HIV but it is not why sharing needles transmits it - many viruses with very different genomes are spread the same way.
steps: Transmission depends on contact with infected blood, not on having an RNA genome
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the structure, not the route, of transmission, so A is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', AIDS
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: After a deep wound, a child is given an injection of preformed antibodies (antitoxin) against tetanus. Some weeks later, the same child is given the tetanus vaccine. Which of the following correctly compares the two?

options.text: Both give active immunity with memory cells
The antitoxin gives active immunity; the vaccine gives passive immunity
The antitoxin gives quick passive immunity without memory; the vaccine gives active immunity and generates memory B and T-cells
Both give passive immunity, because both are injected

solution.explanation: Injecting preformed antibodies gives passive immunity: the response is quick, but the child's own lymphocytes are not stimulated, so no memory is formed. A vaccine gives active immunity: the child produces its own antibodies, which is slower, and memory B and T-cells are formed for a quick response later.
steps: Vaccine -> active: slower, memory cells formed
solution.why_others_wrong: The route (injection) does not decide the type; what matters is whether antibodies are supplied ready-made (passive) or made by the body (active).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Active and passive immunity; Vaccination and immunisation
solution.final_answer: Option C: The antitoxin gives quick passive immunity without memory; the vaccine gives active immunity and generates memory B and T-cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage in the life cycle of Plasmodium) with List-II (site where it occurs).

List-I:
A. Storage of sporozoites
B. First asexual reproduction after entering a human
C. Development of gametocytes (sexual stages)
D. Fertilisation and development of gametes

List-II:
I. Red blood cells of the human
II. Stomach of the female Anopheles mosquito
III. Salivary glands of the female Anopheles mosquito
IV. Liver cells of the human

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

solution.concept: Sites in the life cycle of Plasmodium
solution.explanation: NCERT: sporozoites are stored in the salivary glands of the mosquito and enter a human through its bite. The parasites reproduce asexually first in liver cells and then attack the RBCs. Sexual stages (gametocytes) develop in the RBCs. When a female Anopheles takes up gametocytes with the blood meal, fertilisation and development take place in the mosquito's stomach.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the salivary glands with the stomach, the liver with the RBCs, or the RBCs with the mosquito's stomach.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common diseases in humans (malaria)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Drugs such as anti-histamines quickly reduce the symptoms of an allergy.
Reason (R): The symptoms of allergic reactions are caused by the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the mast cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the allergic reaction is due to the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the mast cells; the use of drugs like anti-histamine, adrenalin and steroids quickly reduces the symptoms. Because histamine released by mast cells causes the symptoms, a drug that counters histamine relieves them, so R explains A.
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the cause on which the anti-histamine acts, so B is wrong; both are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Allergies
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are secondary lymphoid organs?

(a) Spleen
(b) Lymph nodes
(c) Tonsils
(d) Peyer's patches of the small intestine
(e) Thymus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (e) only
(c), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary lymphoid organs are the bone marrow and thymus, where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. After maturation the lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs such as spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of the small intestine and appendix, where they interact with the antigen and proliferate to become effector cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ, so any option including (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Lymphoid organs
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In an HIV-infected person, the number of helper T-lymphocytes falls progressively. Which immune function is weakened as a result?

options.text: Only the physical barriers of innate immunity, such as the skin
Both antibody production by B-cells and cell-mediated immunity, since helper T-cells are needed for both
Only the secretion of acid in the stomach
Neither, because B-cells produce antibodies without any help

solution.explanation: NCERT: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies; T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B-cells produce them, and T-lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity. HIV attacks helper T-lymphocytes (TH) and progressively decreases their number, so the person becomes immunodeficient: both antibody production (which needs T-cell help) and cell-mediated responses suffer.
steps: Helper T-cells help B-cells make antibodies
Loss of TH cells weakens both -> immunodeficiency
solution.why_others_wrong: Skin and stomach acid are innate barriers not dependent on helper T-cells; NCERT states that T-cells help B-cells produce antibodies, so B-cell function does suffer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', AIDS; Acquired immunity
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both antibody production by B-cells and cell-mediated immunity, since helper T-cells are needed for both

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Misuse of anabolic steroids in females can cause abnormal menstrual cycles and excessive hair growth on the face and body.
Statement II: In males, misuse of anabolic steroids can cause breast enlargement and has the potential for kidney and liver dysfunction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in females, side-effects of anabolic steroids include masculinisation, increased aggressiveness, mood swings, depression, abnormal menstrual cycles, excessive hair growth on the face and body, enlargement of the clitoris and deepening of voice. In males they include acne, aggressiveness, mood swings, depression, reduction of size of the testicles, decreased sperm production, potential for kidney and liver dysfunction, breast enlargement, premature baldness and enlargement of the prostate gland.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are from NCERT's list, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Drugs; Adolescence and drug/alcohol abuse
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In bioprocess engineering, for producing antibiotics, vaccines and enzymes on a large scale, it is necessary to maintain:

options.text: A sterile (microbial contamination-free) ambience, so that only the desired microbe or cell grows
A mixed culture of many microbes, so that the yield increases
A temperature close to 0 °C throughout the process
Complete absence of oxygen in every bioprocess

solution.explanation: NCERT: bioprocess engineering means maintenance of a sterile (microbial contamination-free) ambience in chemical engineering processes to enable growth of only the desired microbe/eukaryotic cell in large quantities for the manufacture of biotechnological products like antibiotics, vaccines and enzymes.
steps: Large-scale culture of only the desired cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Contaminating microbes would compete with the desired cells; NCERT does not require near-freezing temperature or absence of oxygen (stirred-tank bioreactors actually supply oxygen).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option A: A sterile (microbial contamination-free) ambience, so that only the desired microbe or cell grows

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: EcoRI recognises 5'-GAATTC-3' and cuts each strand between the bases G and A. How many unpaired (single-stranded) nucleotides are present in the overhang of each sticky end so produced?

solution.explanation: Upper strand 5'-G|AATTC-3' and lower strand 3'-CTTAA|G-5' are cut between G and A. The single-stranded stretch left on each end is AATT, i.e., 4 nucleotides. These overhanging stretches are the sticky ends, which form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts.
steps: Cut after G on both strands
solution.shortcut: Overhang length = site length - 2 x (bases before the cut) = 6 - 2 = 4.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 counts the whole recognition site; 2 halves the overhang; 1 counts only the G that stays on one side.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: 4

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In genetic engineering, restriction endonucleases are used to form:

options.text: Proteins from amino acids
Recombinant molecules of DNA composed of DNA from different genomes
RNA copies of genes for translation
Primers for PCR

solution.explanation: NCERT: restriction endonucleases are used in genetic engineering to form 'recombinant' molecules of DNA, which are composed of DNA from different genomes.
steps: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites
Fragments from different genomes are joined -> recombinant DNA
solution.why_others_wrong: Restriction enzymes act on DNA; they do not make proteins or RNA, and primers are chemically synthesised oligonucleotides.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Recombinant molecules of DNA composed of DNA from different genomes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, in almost all recombinant technologies the ultimate aim is to:

options.text: Destroy the host bacterium
Remove all plasmids from the host cell
Make the host resistant to all antibiotics
Produce a desirable protein

solution.explanation: NCERT: in almost all recombinant technologies, the ultimate aim is to produce a desirable protein. A protein-encoding gene expressed in a heterologous host gives a recombinant protein.
steps: Made in a heterologous host -> recombinant protein
solution.why_others_wrong: The host is used, not destroyed; plasmids are vectors, not something to remove; antibiotic resistance genes are only selectable markers, not the aim.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Obtaining the foreign gene product
solution.final_answer: Option D: Produce a desirable protein

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Restriction enzymes belong to the class of enzymes called nucleases. Exonucleases, one type of nuclease, remove nucleotides from:

options.text: Specific positions within the DNA
Only RNA molecules
The middle of a palindromic sequence only
The ends of the DNA

solution.explanation: NCERT: nucleases are of two kinds - exonucleases and endonucleases. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
steps: Endo- : within the DNA, at specific positions
solution.why_others_wrong: Cutting at specific positions within DNA is what endonucleases do; nucleases named here act on DNA, not only RNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: The ends of the DNA

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A 12 kb linear DNA molecule has EcoRI sites at 3 kb and at 8 kb from its left end. It is completely digested with EcoRI and run on an agarose gel. Which fragment moves farthest from the well?

options.text: The 5 kb fragment
The 4 kb fragment
All fragments stay together as one band
The 3 kb fragment

solution.explanation: Cutting at 3 kb and 8 kb gives fragments of 3 kb (0-3), 5 kb (3-8) and 4 kb (8-12). In agarose gel electrophoresis DNA fragments separate according to size by the sieving effect of the gel; the smaller the fragment, the farther it moves. So the 3 kb fragment moves farthest.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 kb is the largest and moves least; 4 kb lies between; fragments of different sizes do separate into different bands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Separation and isolation of DNA fragments (gel electrophoresis)
solution.final_answer: Option D: The 3 kb fragment

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Bacterial cells treated with a specific concentration of calcium can take up recombinant DNA.
Reason (R): Divalent cations increase the efficiency with which DNA enters the bacterium through pores in its cell wall.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: since DNA is hydrophilic, it cannot pass through cell membranes. The bacterial cells are made competent by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium, which increases the efficiency with which DNA enters the bacterium through pores in its cell wall. That increased efficiency is exactly why calcium-treated cells take up DNA.
steps: Calcium (divalent cation) increases DNA entry -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the reason for A, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Competent host (for transformation with recombinant DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The presence of more than one recognition site for a restriction enzyme within a vector will generate several fragments, which will complicate gene cloning.
Statement II: In selection by insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase, colonies carrying the recombinant DNA give a blue colour with the chromogenic substrate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: to link the alien DNA, the vector needs very few, preferably single, recognition sites; more than one site generates several fragments and complicates cloning. With insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase, non-recombinant colonies give blue colour, whereas recombinant colonies do not produce any colour.
steps: Statement II: false - recombinant colonies are colourless
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses the colours, so A and D are wrong; Statement I is true, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (requirement in an experiment) with List-II (technique used).

List-I:
A. Making multiple copies of a gene in vitro
B. Separating DNA fragments according to size
C. Injecting recombinant DNA directly into the nucleus of an animal cell
D. Bombarding plant cells with DNA-coated gold or tungsten micro-particles

List-II:
I. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR)
II. Biolistics (gene gun)
III. Agarose gel electrophoresis
IV. Micro-injection

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

solution.explanation: PCR synthesises multiple copies of a gene in vitro using primers and DNA polymerase. Agarose gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size. In micro-injection, recombinant DNA is injected directly into the nucleus of an animal cell. In biolistics (gene gun), cells are bombarded with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA; it is suitable for plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap PCR with electrophoresis, micro-injection with biolistics, or electrophoresis with micro-injection.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification using PCR; Gel electrophoresis; Competent host

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following features are required in a vector to facilitate cloning?

(a) An origin of replication (ori)
(b) A selectable marker
(c) Cloning sites (recognition sites for restriction enzymes)
(d) A gene for the Bt toxin
(e) A large number of recognition sites for the same restriction enzyme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b) and (d) only
(a), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: the features required to facilitate cloning into a vector are the origin of replication (ori), a selectable marker and cloning sites (very few, preferably single, recognition sites for the commonly used restriction enzymes); vectors for plants and animals are also needed for those hosts. A Bt toxin gene is a gene that may be cloned, not a vector feature, and many sites for one enzyme would cut the vector into several fragments.
solution.why_others_wrong: A vector needs very few recognition sites, not many, and the Bt gene is not a vector feature, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A scientist wants to introduce recombinant DNA into plant cells without using any 'disarmed pathogen' vector. Which method, described by NCERT as suitable for plants, should be used?

options.text: Micro-injection into the nucleus of an animal cell
Biolistics (gene gun)
Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Disarmed retrovirus

solution.explanation: NCERT: in biolistics (gene gun), cells are bombarded with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA; this method is suitable for plants. Micro-injection injects DNA directly into the nucleus of an animal cell. Agrobacterium and retroviruses are disarmed pathogen vectors, which the scientist wants to avoid.
solution.why_others_wrong: Micro-injection is described for animal cells; Agrobacterium and retroviruses are pathogen-based vectors.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Competent host (for transformation with recombinant DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Biolistics (gene gun)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a continuous culture system, the used medium is drained out from one side while fresh medium is added from the other.
Statement II: A continuous culture system maintains the cells in their physiologically most active log/exponential phase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the continuous culture system, the used medium is drained out from one side while fresh medium is added from the other to maintain the cells in their physiologically most active log/exponential phase. This produces a larger biomass and higher yields of the desired protein.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT lines, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Obtaining the foreign gene product
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A PCR is started with 5 double-stranded molecules of a DNA segment. If every cycle exactly doubles the number of molecules, what is the minimum number of cycles needed to obtain at least 1000 molecules?

solution.explanation: After n cycles the number of molecules is 5 x 2^n. 5 x 2^7 = 640 (less than 1000) and 5 x 2^8 = 1280 (at least 1000). So 8 cycles are the minimum.
solution.why_others_wrong: 7 cycles give only 640; 10 ignores the 5 starting molecules (2^10 = 1024); 200 treats the increase as linear (1000/5).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option B: 8

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Agarose gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to their size.
Reason (R): Agarose is a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Basis of separation versus source of agarose
solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through the sieving effect provided by the agarose gel. Agarose is a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds. Its source is a true fact but does not explain size-based separation; the sieving effect does.
steps: Separation is due to sieving, not to where agarose comes from
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the origin of the matrix, not the reason for separation, so A is wrong; both are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Separation and isolation of DNA fragments (gel electrophoresis)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (enzyme) with List-II (action in recombinant DNA work).

List-I:
A. Restriction endonuclease
B. Ribonuclease
C. DNA ligase
D. Thermostable DNA polymerase

List-II:
I. Joins the cut ends of the vector and the foreign DNA
II. Extends the primers using nucleotides and the template during PCR
III. Cuts DNA at a specific recognition sequence
IV. Removes RNA from the DNA preparation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

solution.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific recognition (palindromic) sequences. Ribonuclease removes RNA during isolation of DNA. DNA ligase joins the cut vector and the source DNA. A thermostable DNA polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus) extends the primers in PCR, remaining active at the high temperature used for denaturation.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the restriction enzyme with ligase, ribonuclease with the polymerase, or the restriction enzyme with ribonuclease.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology; Processes of recombinant DNA technology
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A gene and a plasmid vector are each cut with EcoRI and then mixed with DNA ligase. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The gene and the vector get the same kind of sticky ends, so they can be joined.
(b) The sticky ends form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts, which facilitates the action of DNA ligase.
(c) The vector should preferably have a single EcoRI site, so that it is not cut into several fragments.
(d) If the gene had been cut with a different restriction enzyme, its ends would always match the EcoRI ends of the vector.
(e) DNA ligase cuts the DNA at the sequence GAATTC.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (d) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.concept: Joining DNA cut by the same enzyme
solution.explanation: NCERT: when cut by the same restriction enzyme, the resultant DNA fragments have the same kind of sticky ends, which can be joined end-to-end using DNA ligases; the sticky ends form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts, which facilitates ligase action. Normally the vector and source DNA must be cut with the same enzyme; a vector needs very few, preferably single, recognition sites. Ligase joins DNA; it does not cut it.
steps: (d) false - different enzymes generally give different ends
(e) false - cutting is done by the restriction enzyme
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement (d) ignores the need to use the same enzyme and (e) gives the cutting role to ligase, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes; Cutting of DNA at specific locations
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase lets recombinants be selected on a single plate, unlike inactivation of an antibiotic resistance gene, which needs plating on two plates with different antibiotics.
Statement II: If many copies of the target DNA are wanted, it should be cloned in a vector whose origin of replication supports a high copy number.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: selection of recombinants by inactivation of an antibiotic resistance gene is cumbersome because it requires simultaneous plating on two plates having different antibiotics; therefore alternative markers such as β-galactosidase, which give colour with a chromogenic substrate, have been developed. The ori controls the copy number of the linked DNA, so a high-copy vector is chosen to get many copies of the target DNA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In gene therapy, a normal gene is delivered into the individual or embryo in order to:

options.text: Take over the function of, and compensate for, the non-functional gene
Destroy all the cells that carry the defective gene
Produce antibodies against the defective gene
Convert the person into a transgenic animal model of the disease

solution.explanation: NCERT: gene therapy involves delivery of a normal gene into the individual or embryo to take over the function of and compensate for the non-functional gene.
steps: It takes over the function of, and compensates for, the faulty gene
solution.why_others_wrong: Gene therapy compensates for the faulty gene; it does not kill cells, raise antibodies, or create disease models (that is a use of transgenic animals).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose that, in the RNAi strategy against Meloidegyne incognitia, the introduced nematode-specific DNA produced only sense RNA in the tobacco cells and no anti-sense RNA. What would be the most likely result?

options.text: The sense RNA alone would silence the nematode mRNA even more effectively
The tobacco plant's own mRNA would be silenced instead
The plant would start producing Bt toxin
No dsRNA would form, so RNAi would not be initiated and the plant would not be protected

solution.explanation: NCERT: the introduction of DNA produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells. These two RNAs, being complementary to each other, formed a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that initiated RNAi and silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode. Without anti-sense RNA, no dsRNA forms, so RNAi is not initiated and the nematode mRNA is not silenced.
steps: No anti-sense -> no dsRNA -> no silencing
solution.why_others_wrong: Silencing requires a complementary dsRNA, which needs both strands; nothing in the set-up targets the plant's own mRNA; Bt toxin genes are not involved in this strategy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option D: No dsRNA would form, so RNAi would not be initiated and the plant would not be protected
